title: Blue Origin is going all in on the New Glenn rocket
summary: Blue Origin is ramping up development of its New Glenn rocket with infrastructure designed to enable multiple flights per week by 2030, marking a major expansion of the company's launch capabilities.
content: The infrastructure is designed to support multiple flights per week by the end of the decade.

content: Android laptops are here, but Google has a lot of work ahead to make them good.

title: Time is a-changin’: say goodbye to the leap second
summary: The International Bureau of Weights and Measures voted to eliminate the leap second effective May 20, 2027—accelerated from the originally planned 2035 deadline—to prevent infrastructure failures similar to Y2K concerns.
content:
An important change will soon be made to global timekeeping that aims to prevent potential infrastructure failures akin to the Y2K bug scare. On Thursday, the International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM) voted to scrap the leap second, an ad hoc time adjustment that's occasionally added so tracked time standards mirror the Earth's real (and inconsistent) rotation.

title: Even Benchmark thinks AI is eroding the venture pact against backing rivals
summary: Venture capital firm Benchmark acknowledges that AI-driven competition and portfolio pressures are making it increasingly difficult for VCs to maintain the traditional agreement against backing competing startups.
content: Benchmark says the Valley’s rule against backing rivals is getting harder to keep.

title: The Tesla Roadster flew, drove upside down, and hit 60mph in under a second
summary: Tesla demonstrated its next-generation Roadster in Texas, where it flew, drove upside down, and accelerated to 60mph in under a second, though the demo lacked production details like price or release date. The hypercar is promised for 2028 production but faces significant real-world challenges.
content:
Elon Musk promised a flying car. And the Tesla Roadster did exactly that. 
Tesla demonstrated its next-generation Roadster at an event in Waco, Texas, where the electric supercar drove upside down, briefly flew, and accelerated to 60mph in under a second. It was an impressive demonstration of a car that likely will come with some heavy caveats and restrictions if it ever goes into production.

title: Tesla reveals SpaceX-powered Roadster that flies and falls with style
summary: Tesla showcased a Roadster equipped with SpaceX thrusters that leaped over multiple vehicle models including the Cybercab, Cybertruck, and Tesla Semi during a Texas demonstration.
content: The new car used thrusters to leap over a Cybercab, Cybertruck, Tesla Semi, Model Y, and Model 3 at a demo in Texas.
